summary: Execution nodes trust receptor connections signed by a CA; the operator generates a self-signed CA unless you create a TLS secret named <controller CR name>-receptor-ca from your ca.crt and ca.key and, if controller is already deployed, restart its deployment. Changing the CA makes existing execution nodes unavailable until you re-run their install bundles.
questions: How do I use my own CA for automation mesh on OpenShift?
Why are execution nodes unavailable after changing the receptor CA?

answer_card.title: Custom receptor CA on the operator
answer_card.answer_md:
1. Create the secret, named `<Controller CR name>-receptor-ca`:
   ```
   kubectl create secret tls <controller-cr>-receptor-ca \
     --cert=/path/to/ca.crt --key=/path/to/ca.key
   ```
2. If controller is already deployed: `kubectl rollout restart deployment <controller-cr>`

Changing the CA breaks existing execution nodes. Download and re-run each node's install bundle to get certificates from the new CA; nodes become ready after a few minutes.
